feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong senior digital/public-sector CV with clear positioning, credible progression, and solid evidence of scope. It reads professionally and is largely error-free, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style/grammar inconsistencies that reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: progression at NACo shows increasing responsibility and supports the “Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader” brand well.  
- Good credibility signals: concrete scale metrics (10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers) make impact more believable.  
- Broad, relevant skill mix: strategy, platforms, analytics, governance, multimedia, and AI are aligned to target senior digital roles.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce repetition and tighten structure: “Topline Skills,” “Core Competencies,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to avoid redundancy and save space.  
- Add more outcome-focused achievements: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than results; include measurable improvements in engagement, efficiency, adoption, or cost savings.  
- Fix style consistency issues: use consistent punctuation in lists; “social, and multimedia” should be “social and multimedia”; “A2/Learning” is awkward—use “A2 (learning)”; consider standardizing title case and date formatting. No major misspellings found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear seniority and domain focus. It reads well, but it’s slightly dense and overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten to one sharper value proposition and foreground the most relevant differentiators: public-sector scale, enterprise web modernization, and governance/analytics leadership.
- Replace “building the platforms” with more direct, active phrasing; “high-volume public-sector communications” could be simplified to “large-scale public-sector communications.”
- Consider trimming lower-priority items like multimedia production from the intro, since they are covered elsewhere and dilute the core leadership narrative.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience leading enterprise web modernization, governance, and content operations for large-scale public-sector communications. Builds and scales digital platforms, analytics infrastructure, and editorial systems that improve publishing efficiency, audience insight, and user experience across complex, mission-driven organizations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with core competencies, recent projects, and current consulting work; mention it only if targeting AI-forward roles.
- “Multimedia production” is already well supported in work experience and skills, so it may not need intro-level emphasis.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. It would be stronger if tightened into broader, less repetitive capability areas with more parallel phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use shorter, category-style phrases and keep structure parallel; e.g.: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and optimization • Multi-channel communications leadership
- Replace weaker/general wording like “platform integration” and “content experiences” with sharper terms tied to the CV, such as CMS modernization, search, automation, or audience discovery
- Consider emphasizing the most marketable recent strengths: AI-enabled search, Drupal/CMS modernization, analytics infrastructure, and governance
- Suggested rewrite: Enterprise web and CMS modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and optimization infrastructure • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and systems integration • Multi-channel public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” and “Multi-channel communications operations” overlap with the header and Topline Skills
- “Digital governance & editorial systems” closely repeats language already used in the header and work experience
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshots, but the footer currently repeats achievements already covered in Work Experience and reads a bit dense. Tightening phrasing and emphasizing distinct outcomes or formats will make it feel more additive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add dates or “Selected recent projects” framing to reinforce recency and context.
- Use parallel, tighter verbs: “Created,” “Launched,” “Developed,” “Produced,” and trim stacked nouns.
- Clarify one distinctive result or purpose per project, e.g., “to improve policy-content discovery” or “to support ongoing campaign expansion.”
- Standardize style: use “10-by-20-foot” instead of “10×20-foot,” and consider “AI-powered” or “AI-enabled” consistently across the CV.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI Hybrid Search,” microsite work, and the advocacy video series substantially overlap with current freelance and NACo bullets; keep this section more portfolio-style or more specific than the experience entries.
- “Built/Developed” repeats heavily; vary wording to avoid sounding formulaic.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, skills, and project footer. Make it sharper by foregrounding scope, technical leadership, and any concrete outcomes.

Suggested edit
- Open with a tighter summary: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements across web, campaigns, content operations, and AI-enabled discovery.”
- Convert bullets to impact-led phrasing: “Built organization-wide workflows, analytics, and governance systems to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia teams.”
- Combine overlapping Drupal/CMS bullets: “Designed and launched Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components, downloadable toolkits, and front-end/CMS enhancements for high-traffic public sites.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages/users, faster publishing, reduced support issues, improved search success, engagement lifts, or adoption across teams.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “AI-enabled search initiative” duplicates the Recent Projects section; keep this bullet high-level here and let the footer carry detail.
- Governance/analytics/workflows also echo the header and NACo role; emphasize what is new in this engagement.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. Tighten the opening, foreground the biggest transformation outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management details covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web modernization, analytics, governance, multimedia production, and budget/team operations.”
- Combine and prioritize the strongest achievement: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make outcomes more explicit where possible: add % improvements in publishing speed, reporting adoption, engagement, cost savings, or reduced vendor reliance from the studio build.
- Tighten weaker bullets: replace “Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels…” with a more outcome-led line on audience growth, campaign performance, or executive visibility.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this role focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video production/studio language may overlap with older NACo roles unless framed here as building institutional capacity.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry reads generic and overlaps with both the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager/Producer role. Make it more execution-focused and quantify scale/results where possible.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + ownership: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, supporting advocacy messaging and organization-wide editorial execution.”
- Tighten bullets to concrete responsibilities: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Reframe video bullet around growth/impact: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.” Add views, open/click lift, or production cadence if available.
- Combine planning/workflow bullets into one stronger line: “Built more consistent editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving coordination and content delivery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Helping scale” and “helped improve” sound soft; use direct ownership to avoid blending into adjacent NACo roles.
- Video program language overlaps with the 2015–2018 role and Recent Projects; distinguish this role as scaling/operationalizing, not launching.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. Tighten it to emphasize leadership scope and strategic value rather than broad phrases.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic labels with sharper, differentiated terms:
- Enterprise digital strategy & operating models
- Editorial governance, publishing standards & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector, membership & advocacy messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Use parallel phrasing; avoid mixing nouns (“strategy”) with adjectives (“audience-focused”).
- Consider dropping “content planning,” which feels junior compared with the seniority shown elsewhere.
- If space allows, add one higher-impact qualifier such as “for high-volume, mission-driven organizations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” repeat Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” is already reinforced in the header and multiple NACo roles.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize platform leadership and execution themes tied to recent Drupal/CMS modernization work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Drupal and enterprise CMS delivery” instead of just “Drupal.”
- Prioritize recent, differentiating strengths: Drupal, CMS modernization, API integrations, workflow automation, AI-enabled search.
- De-emphasize older/basic items by grouping them: “Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery).”
- Suggested rewrite: “- Drupal and enterprise CMS delivery - CMS modernization and migration - API integrations and workflow automation - Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) - Airtable-based content systems - SharePoint, WordPress and Power Pages - AI-enabled search experiences”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Drupal,” “WordPress,” “SharePoint,” and coding languages are repeated in “Technical + IT”; keep this section higher-level.
- “Workflow automation” and “AI-enabled search experiences” also echo Core Competencies, so use shorter phrasing here.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a generic inventory. Tighten it around strategic analytics leadership and avoid repeating the fuller “Technical + IT” section.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Analytics strategy, reporting & optimization.”
- Suggested rewrite: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio & Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework design • Executive/leadership dashboarding • SEO, UX and performance analysis”
- Put the highest-value, most recent strengths first: analytics strategy, KPI design, dashboarding, then tools.
- If you have metrics, reflect them elsewhere in experience bullets rather than here; keep this section concise and scannable.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; consider making Topline Skills more strategic and leaving the full tool stack below.
- “Leadership reporting” overlaps with “analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies; “executive dashboarding” is sharper.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize delivery capability and recent leadership-level multimedia work rather than listing basic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to **Multimedia Production, Studio & Event Delivery** for a more senior, outcomes-oriented tone.
- Replace generic items with sharper phrasing: **Broadcast-quality video production**, **Livestream and hybrid event delivery**, **PTZ camera and studio systems**, **Virtual event production workflows**.
- If space allows, add one impact cue tied to recent work, e.g. **Built and operated in-house studio capabilities for advocacy programming and live events**.
- Keep to 4 bullets max and avoid software/tool detail here since that already appears in Technical + IT.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- **Livestream operations** already appears in Core Competencies; use **livestream and hybrid event delivery** here or remove one version.
- **Video production and editing** overlaps with **Premiere Pro / podcast production / livestream studio workflows** in Technical + IT; keep this section focused on capability, not tools.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too generic and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Use it to signal depth and recency—especially Drupal—rather than repeat a simple platform list.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to emphasize strongest/current platforms first: **Drupal (enterprise migrations, modular microsites)** • **WordPress** • **SharePoint / Power Pages** • **GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add proficiency context instead of just names: e.g., **Drupal (primary CMS; large public-sector sites)** • **WordPress (campaign/editorial sites)** • **SharePoint / Power Pages (internal/business apps)**
- Consider renaming the heading to **CMS Platforms** or **Web Platforms** for tighter phrasing.
- If GitHub Pages was only lightly used, move it to a secondary tools line or drop it to keep focus on higher-value enterprise platforms.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; differentiate this section by adding usage context or consolidate.
- Avoid repeating “CMS modernization” here since it already appears in Topline Skills and work experience.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation-level tools that support recent Drupal, analytics, and automation work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename/refocus to: **Front-End & Technical Implementation:** HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions
- Standardize phrasing for clarity and seniority: use **JavaScript** instead of mixing markup versions unless ATS requires them; consider **HTML/CSS** rather than **HTML5/CSS3**
- If true, add scope qualifiers: **custom front-end implementation**, **tag deployment**, **serverless scripting**, **deployment automation**
- Stronger version: **HTML/CSS • JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions (deployment/workflow automation)**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Repeats **HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery** and **API integrations** from Topline Skills; keep detail here and shorten the Topline version.
- GTM may also overlap with analytics/tooling; consider moving it under Data/Analytics if that section needs more depth.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems leadership. Since “workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear elsewhere, this item should be tighter and more systems-oriented.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe by function, not just brand names: “Workflow automation & work management: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier; Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp; Slack, Microsoft Teams.”
- Put strongest/relevant tools first based on recent work: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira/Asana.
- If space allows, add light context to show application: “used for editorial planning, approvals, cross-team coordination, and process automation.”
- Consider dropping one or two lower-value tools if not central (e.g., Basecamp, Trello) to keep the list sharper.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Slack and Teams are collaboration tools more than workflow systems; consider moving them to a separate “Collaboration” line if you need cleaner categorization.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tools, but this item is too bare compared with the rest of the CV and misses a chance to signal scale and strategic use. It should emphasize enterprise email/engagement platforms rather than read like a generic software list.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Reorder by likely relevance/scale: **Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope in brief: **enterprise newsletter operations, member communications, journey/campaign automation**
- Example rewrite: **Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Mailchimp — enterprise email newsletters, member engagement campaigns, and automated audience journeys**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work experience already showing email leadership; avoid adding claims here that repeat “tens of thousands” unless you remove or tighten them elsewhere.
- “Engagement” is broad; don’t imply CRM ownership unless you directly administered segmentation, automation, or journey design.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool set, but this line is generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” In a recent-seniority CV, this section should stay lean, tool-focused, and avoid repeating broader capability language already proven in the NACo role.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • A/B testing**
- Replace **SEO** with **Google Search Console** if that’s the actual tool; keep this section tool/platform-based rather than mixing in disciplines.
- Replace **Dashboarding** with nothing, or with a specific platform already listed; dashboarding is an outcome/capability, not a tool.
- Order by strongest/recently evidenced tools from work experience: GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Clarity.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates **Topline Skills: Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider trimming one of the two or making this one strictly tools-only.
- “A/B testing” is fine here only if not emphasized elsewhere; otherwise it may read as filler without a quantified example in experience.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but this reads broadly and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with concrete scope or outputs if you can.

Suggested edit
- Reframe around early-team building and hands-on production: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add 1–2 measurable outcomes if available: website refresh scope, livestream/event volume, weekly video cadence, audience growth, or team support.
- Tighten the second sentence to emphasize execution: “Supported a major website refresh; produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates; and provided day-to-day oversight to a digital media associate.”
- Consider splitting into 2 bullets for scanability rather than one dense paragraph.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on launching/building the program, not expanding it.
- “Strengthening workflows” and “guidance to a digital media associate” echo later leadership themes; use lighter wording here to avoid repeating management language.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a notable “first podcast” achievement, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Tighten it to emphasize innovation/program support and the podcast launch as the standout result.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the unique contribution: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives that supported NACo program development and policy communications.”
- Make the podcast launch the second sentence and sharpen ownership: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- Trim generic phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials”; replace with a more specific support function or output if known.
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of episodes launched, audience growth, or types/scale of research projects supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; avoid repeating broad multimedia language.
- Don’t overstate web/email/social responsibilities here, since those are better established in more recent NACo positions.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills list, but it reads more like a mix of software and capabilities. Tighten it into a cleaner tools-focused line and avoid repeating broader multimedia strengths already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as primarily software/platforms, not functions: “Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator”
